passages.heard: This woman is shooting dried peas at a stranger's bedroom window at four in the morning,  and he's paying her to do it!
Before cheap alarm clocks, British workers hired a knocker upper, a human alarm clock  walking the dark streets with a long pole, or, in Mary Smith's case, a pea shooter.
You see, it worked like a snooze button.  You can't switch off.  P after P rattles the glass  and she doesn't move on until somebody comes to the window.
Her customers paid a few pence a week, and she woke whole streets of London's East End  before sunrise.  Her daughter Molly took over and kept going into the Second World War.
So, who woke up the knocker-upper?  Usually nobody.  Most of them stayed up all night working, then slept through the day.
